business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Student Placement and Golden Visa Residence Advisory

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (national territory, no sub-state tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain-China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 2005, in force 2008)
Spain-Colombia Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force as relevant)
Convention between Spain and the United States for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1990)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y financiación del terrorismo, as amended by Royal Decree-Law 7/2021; Royal Decree 304/2014, of 5 May, approving the Regulation of Law 10/2010; Circular 1/2022 of SEPBLAC; and Articles 31 and 32 of Royal Decree 1/2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital) for registration of ultimate beneficial owners.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the shareholder's passport (Copia autenticada del pasaporte)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing for corporate shareholders (Certificado de estar al corriente en el cumplimiento de las obligaciones sociales)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registry or Companies House of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states) and sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial Power of Attorney for incorporation representative (Poder Notarial para la constitución)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the principal's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states) and sworn Spanish translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence under Law 10/2010 requires screening against the Spanish PEP list (RELEPEP), EU consolidated terrorist financing sanctions, UK HMT and UN Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, and domestic SEPBLAC risk indicators. Before incorporation, a negative screening certificate must be obtained for all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories. On-going transaction monitoring applies during the formation and licensing phase; any PEP or sanctions designation triggers immediate filing to SEPBLAC and suspension of incorporation procedures.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) – online name clearance application via the Colegio de Registradores de España portal (https://www.registradores.org)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Spanish or any of Spain's co-official languages; foreign-language names must be rendered in Latin script and phonetically transliterated into Spanish. The name must be distinctive, not identical or confusingly similar to existing companies, and must comply with Article 402 of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital). Terms such as S.L., S.A., etc., must be appended in the corresponding abbreviated form.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: España or Spain (requires prior Ministry of Foreign Affairs authorization)
Gobierno, Estado, Ayuntamiento, Ministerio (public administrative terms requiring authorization)
Banco, Bank, Financiera (requires Ministry of Economy and Competitiveness approval)
Universidad, Instituto, Fundación (requires relevant educational authority consent)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Mercantil Central rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a new application with alternative names (up to 5) without additional cost. A formal administrative appeal may be lodged within one month to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (ex-DGRN) setting out grounds under the Spanish Companies Act. In practice, resubmission is faster. Extension of a negative name certificate is granted upon application before expiry, extending the validity for an additional 90 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted. A virtual office can serve for correspondence and fiscal notifications, but for the study abroad immigration visa consultancy activity (ISIC 7810), the regulatory authority (Ministry of Migration and Citizenship or designated licensing body) requires a physical, staffed office within the Spanish territory for client files, appointment attendance, and inspection access. A virtual address without operational substance will likely be rejected for the statutory operating license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — quantified risk 70%. Law 10/2010 and sectoral consumer protection rules authorize SEPBLAC and the licensing authority to conduct unannounced physical inspections, particularly for companies handling immigration and visa advisory with cross-border client money.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation certificate (certificación de denominación social)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Central / Colegio de Registradores de España

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff according to share capital and deed complexity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Registry registration fee (inscripción en el Registro Mercantil Provincial)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff based on nominal share capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO disclosure filing and AML pre-incorporation due diligence compliance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish company registry agents / corporate legal counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for AML compliance and beneficial ownership registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation and legalization of foreign documentation (passports, POA, certificates)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish sworn translator and competent foreign authority (apostille)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory translator tariff and official apostille fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation legal counsel and drafting of articles of association (estatutos)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for professional legal services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PIN / NIF application for the new company (código de identificación fiscal)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Alternative/correction fee or administrative handling through appointed legal counsel

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital - LSC): Arts. 12 to 22 (incorporation and formalities), Arts. 23 to 30 (articles of association and registered office), Arts. 102 to 109 (SL minimum capital of EUR 3,000 fully paid-in), Art. 137 (sole administrator) and Arts. 124 to 231 (corporate governance organs).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministerio de Justicia - Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) for the negative name certificate; Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office for the definitive commercial registration of the incorporation deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (public deed of incorporation) submitted electronically through the Registro Mercantil Provincial filing system, evidenced by the registration inscription certificate (certificación de inscripción).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory minimum share capital of EUR 3,000 under Article 4.1 LSC, fully subscribed and paid in cash or in-kind at constitution; founders must deposit the capital in a temporary blocked escrow account at a Spanish credit institution and obtain a bank deposit certificate (certificado de depósito) attached to the notarial deed; the blocked funds are released upon commercial registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED BY THE SOLE FOUNDING MEMBER AS THE FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [●] SOCIEDAD DE RESPONSABILIDAD LIMITADA: (1) Share Subscription - the incorporator hereby ratifies the subscription and full payment of the entire share capital of EUR 3,000, divided into 3,000 shares of EUR 1.00 nominal value each, as evidenced by the bank escrow certificate. (2) Registered Office - the company adopts the address at [●], Madrid, Spain, as its statutory registered office and tax domicile. (3) Officer Appointments - [●] is appointed Sole Administrator and legal representative; [●] is appointed Secretary; both accept office and are granted all corporate powers. (4) Governance - the Board approves opening corporate payment and escrow accounts and authorises filings with the Commercial Registry, the Tax Agency, and Social Security.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Spanish NIE (Foreigner Tax Identification Number)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Police - Oficina de Extranjería (Immigration Office) or Spanish Consulate abroad
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the EX-15 application through the Spanish Consulate or the provincial Oficina de Extranjería; pay the NIE fee (Tasa 012); appear in person for the appointment to obtain the certificate assigning the NIE number; consular issuance avoids the fingerprint step where permitted.
required_dossiers: Letter stating the purpose of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried or refused, correct the EX-15 and fee receipt and re-file; request an expedited consular appointment; appeal administrative denial under Ley 39/2015 or use a legal representative with a notarised power of attorney.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Negative Name Certificate (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) - online name reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File online a petition listing two alternative corporate names for the SL; pay the official tariff; the Central Registry verifies that no identical or confusingly similar name is registered and issues the negative name certificate, valid for six months.
required_dossiers: Name application with two candidate denominations
NIE and passport of the founder(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If all proposed names are rejected on identity or similarity grounds, file a fresh petition with alternative names; the RMC decision may be appealed under the Commercial Registry Regulation, and a new six-month validity period starts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for Provisional Tax ID (NIF Provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - National Tax Agency, census section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Modelo 036 censal declaration electronically or at the local AEAT office, marking the box for a legal entity under formation; the Tax Agency assigns a provisional CIF, which is used for the bank account and the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: NIE and passport of the promoter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the provisional CIF is denied, correct the censal data and resubmit; request urgent assignment at the local AEAT window; provide supporting incorporation documents to cure within 48 hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Escrow Capital Deposit Account and Deposit Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution licensed by the Banco de España
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account titled 'sociedad en constitución' at any Spanish bank; deposit the full share capital of EUR 3,000 and block the funds; obtain the certificado de depósito naming the company in formation and the deposit amount for attachment to the deed.
required_dossiers: Passport and NIE of the account signatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines, select another Spanish credit institution; if the deposit certificate is delayed, request a certified correction; file a delay complaint with the Servicio de Reclamaciones del Banco de España only as a last resort.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Public Deed of Incorporation Before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the district of the registered office (notaría del domicilio social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver to the notary the negative name certificate, bank deposit certificate, provisional CIF, and the draft by-laws (estatutos sociales); the notary verifies legal capacity and consent, authenticates the Escritura Pública de Constitución, and transmits the required copy to the Commercial Registry.
required_dossiers: NIE and passport of the founding member(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses due to by-law defects, amend the estatutos and re-execute; if the deposit certificate is defective, obtain a corrected bank certificate; minor formal issues can be cured without repeating full fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pay Transfer Tax and Stamp Duty (ITP-AJD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Regional Autonomous Community Tax Office (Consejería de Hacienda)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Modelo 600 with the regional tax authority within 30 days of the deed, applying the applicable AJD rate on paid-in capital; obtain the stamped payment certificate (carta de pago) required for registry filing.
required_dossiers: First copy of the public deed of incorporation
Company details and registered office form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the assessment is queried, file a supplementary declaration or rectificación de autoliquidación; for late filing, pay the statutory recargos and interest arrears and request correction under the general tax rules of Ley 58/2003.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Deed at the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the stamped first copy of the deed, the AJD payment certificate, and the registration application (hoja registral) to the Commercial Registry; the registrar examines legality and issues the inscription, after which the company acquires full legal personality and capacity.
required_dossiers: First copy of the notarial deed duly stamped
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a defect note, cure the defects within two months and resubmit, or file a recurso gubernativo before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Definitive NIF and Register with Social Security
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT (definitive NIF) and Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After commercial registration, file the updated Modelo 036 to convert the provisional CIF into the definitive NIF; register the administrator and any employees with the TGSS; activate the corporate operating bank account and the client escrow account required for the wire-transfer and escrow payment rails.
required_dossiers: Certificate of definitive commercial registry registration
Administrator NIE and social security affiliation forms (TA.6/TA.7)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the definitive NIF is withheld, present the commercial registry inscription certificate; if social security affiliation is queried, file the immediate-affiliation request and correct the TA.6/TA.7 forms within the 30-day statutory claim period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local Municipal Council (Ayuntamiento) - Department of Economic Activities and Urban Licensing (Departamento de Actividades Económicas y Licencias Urbanísticas)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Apertura / Licencia de Actividad (Opening and Activity Operating License); for small non-industrial service offices, a prior Declaración Responsable de Actividad may suffice under Ley 12/2012 and municipal ordinances, with formal activity license required for premises with public access.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD) together with the Regional Environmental Department (Consejería de Medio Ambiente) of the relevant autonomous community
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based study-abroad and visa consultancy activities are not listed in Annexes I-II of Ley 21/2013 de Evaluación Ambiental; no full EIA report is required, but the municipal environmental compliance declaration (Declaración Responsable) may require registration for noise and waste aspects of the office premises.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Domestic-grade wastewater discharges complying with the municipal sewer ordinance and RD 1620/2007 reuse limits; negligible VOC and fugitive emissions; commercial packaging and office waste handled under Ley 7/2022 and RD 1055/2022 with separate collection of paper, glass, light packaging and hazardous office waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Código Técnico de la Edificación (CTE DB-SI) and RD 513/2017; structural load and occupancy certificate under CTE DB-SE issued by a licensed architect; workplace health and safety clearance under Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales and RD 486/1997 covering evacuation routes, emergency lighting, fire extinguishers, and safe workstations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic tax procedures are conducted through the AEAT Electronic Office (Sede Electrónica).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a provisional NIF during incorporation and applies for confirmation of its definitive NIF with the AEAT, generally through Modelo 036 and the required incorporation documents. The company must register for relevant tax obligations, including Corporate Income Tax and VAT, through Modelo 036 before commencing taxable activities. A VAT number for intra-Community transactions (NIF-IVA) requires registration in the Register of Intra-Community Operators through Modelo 036 and validation in VIES. A foreign entity without a Spanish establishment generally applies for a Spanish NIF through the AEAT using Modelo 036 and supporting evidence of legal existence and representation; non-EU entities may be required to appoint a Spanish tax representative for VAT purposes, subject to applicable mutual-assistance arrangements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Spanish SL is generally a separate taxpayer subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax. Spain has no US-style check-the-box election for an SL to be treated as a partnership. Applicable hybrid-mismatch rules may deny deductions or require inclusion in income in specified cross-border arrangements; these rules do not constitute an elective entity-classification regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT; Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general domestic turnover threshold: a person carrying out taxable economic activity in Spain is generally required to register for VAT from commencement, subject to statutory exemptions and special regimes. Spain's VAT territory excludes the Canary Islands, Ceuta, and Melilla, which have separate indirect-tax regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not generally require real-time AEAT clearance of every invoice. The Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) system requires specified taxpayers, including businesses exceeding EUR 6,010,121.04 in annual turnover, VAT groups, and taxpayers registered in the monthly refund regime, to transmit invoice-record data electronically, generally within four calendar days subject to statutory exceptions. Certified invoicing-system and electronic-invoicing obligations are subject to applicable implementing rules and transition dates; the general B2B e-invoicing mandate under the Crea y Crece Law is not a universal real-time clearance system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from the Spanish VAT territory to destinations outside the EU are generally exempt with the right to deduct input VAT if the statutory export conditions are met and the supplier retains evidence that the goods left the EU. Intra-Community supplies may be exempt with the right to deduct where the customer is a taxable person identified for VAT in another Member State, the goods are transported there, and the supplier satisfies reporting and evidentiary requirements. Services are not automatically zero-rated as exports: place-of-supply rules determine whether Spanish VAT applies, and statutory exceptions may apply. Immigration, visa, and study-abroad advisory services require transaction-specific analysis of customer status, service characterization, and place of supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration and MRN, with electronic exit-confirmation evidence where available
Commercial invoice and transport evidence, such as a bill of lading, airway bill, or carrier confirmation
Evidence linking the goods and transport documents to the relevant sale and export transaction
Customer VAT identification number and proof of dispatch or arrival in another Member State for an intra-Community supply, where applicable

Bank remittance or payment evidence where relevant to substantiate the transaction; an inward remittance certificate and foreign-exchange repatriation are not general Spanish VAT zero-rating requirements
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain imposes no general foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. Unsupported or improperly claimed VAT exemptions can be reversed through assessment, with recovery of underpaid VAT, late-payment interest, and tax penalties under the General Tax Law. Penalty exposure depends on the conduct and culpability; concealment, false documentation, or other aggravating factors can increase sanctions. Input VAT deductions or refunds attributable to ineligible transactions may also be denied or reclaimed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting jointly with the Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias (SEPBLAC) for AML supervision and with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation for capital-movement policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain applies full euro (EUR) convertibility under Article 63 TFEU. Current-account items are completely liberalized; capital-account transactions (equity, loans, real estate) require only prior statistical declaration (declaración estadística) to the Banco de España via Balance of Payments (BE) forms, not prior authorization. Profit remittance and dividend repatriation are unrestricted but attract 19% withholding tax on dividends and interest (24% on royalties) unless reduced by a tax treaty; cash or bearer-note payments above EUR 10,000 are prohibited under Ley 10/2010. For a study-abroad and golden-visa advisory, incoming client and investor funds must match declared commercial contracts, beneficiary registers, and the corporate purpose to avoid re-characterization as undeclared capital income.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion requirement exists for export or service proceeds in Spain; receipts may be retained in EUR or any foreign currency. However, every transaction with non-residents exceeding EUR 50,000, and all capital movements regardless of amount when so requested by statistics, must be reported to the Banco de España through BE-22/BE-23 statistical declarations within 15 business days. Failure to file exposes the SL to administrative fines under Law 10/2010 and Banco de España Circular procedures.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to Low. Spanish-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) under Law 21/2011 (PSD2) may provide SEPA-only operational payment accounts, but they cannot legally operate escrow or client-money accounts, which under Spanish banking law are reserved to credit institutions. Non-EEA offshore EMIs cannot onboard a Spanish regulated immigration-visa advisory without a Spanish branch or an EEA passport; UK EMIs lost passporting after Brexit and require re-authorization by the Banco de España. Therefore, all escrow and corporate treasury functions must sit at a Tier-1 Spanish bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) because the sector carries a Medium-Risk Enhanced classification. Ley 10/2010 and SEPBLAC guidance require a face-to-face interview for high-risk customer types; remote video onboarding is permitted only where the customer holds an EU-approved digital identity under RDL 7/2021. Non-resident directors must either attend a Spanish branch for an in-person interview or execute a notarized, apostilled power of attorney (poder general) at a Spanish Consulate and appoint a resident attorney-in-fact, who then appears physically at the bank. The bank also demands a validated NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero), the notarial deed of incorporation, and the Mercantile Registry certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector risk: immigration, study-abroad, and golden-visa advisory with client-money flows routed to third parties (universities, embassies, relocation agents).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory license file: registration with the Ministerio de Inclusión, Seguridad Social y Migraciones where applicable, gestor administrativo or notarial appointment of the compliance officer, the SL board-approved AML/CFT manual, SEPBLAC external auditor report, and itemized client service contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident, non-EU majority shareholder or director controlling the SL.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax-residence certificates, CRS/FATCA self-certifications, NIE, notarized board resolutions, apostilled criminal-record certificates (certificado de antecedentes penales) from the country of residence, and 24-month source-of-wealth bank statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Client monies deposited into a general operational account without escrow segregation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A dedicated client-money escrow account titled 'ES_SL Client Money Escrow', bank-executed escrow terms and conditions, weekly client-money ledger and reconciliation reports under Law 5/2015, professional-indemnity insurance certificate, and an annual forensic accountant attestation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or rapid incoming wire transfers from high-risk jurisdictions (LatAm, China, Middle East) funding tuition or golden-visa packages.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original university admission letter or public-authority acceptance, itemized commercial invoice, student/passport identification file, complete know-your-client documentation, SWIFT gpi intermediary-bank trail, and timely BE-22 declaration to the Banco de España.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEPs, sanctioned-touch beneficiaries, or multi-layered UBO structures in the client portfolio.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SEPBLAC PEP screening log, EU/OFSI/UN sanctions screening evidence, enhanced due-diligence questionnaire, Libro Registro de Socios UBO extract, and written approval by the SL compliance officer supported by external counsel opinion.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are routed as SWIFT MT103 to the SL operational account at a Banco de España-supervised credit institution, using the BE-22 direct-investment classification code '2510 - Capital contributions to non-listed resident companies' with narration 'Aportación al capital social de ES_SL'. The bank requires a notarized capital-increase deed, registration in the Mercantile Registry, the injecting shareholder's NIE, a source-of-funds declaration, and proof of payment of the 1% capital-operation tax (Impuesto sobre Transmisiones Patrimoniales y Actos Jurídicos Documentados). Trust and corporate investors must additionally provide a chain-of-ownership chart, CRS self-certification, and home-jurisdiction legal opinion. Student and golden-visa escrow deposits are credited using explicit purpose narration 'Escrow - Study Abroad / Golden Visa' with the escrow agreement attached through the corporate banking portal.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EUR disbursements flow through SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001) within the SEPA zone; non-EUR and SEPA-excluded payments use SWIFT MT103/MT202 with service-purpose code 'S700 - Business services' for balance-of-payments statistics. Payments to universities, embassies, and relocation partners are released only against a valid invoice, admission letter, or signed escrow disbursement instruction. Commercial letters of credit (UCP 600, SWIFT MT700) are reserved for bulk institutional contracts where the counterparty mandates LC terms. All disbursements above EUR 10,000 pass through enhanced transaction monitoring and require a pre-validated beneficiary master file and recurring-payment mandate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD and EUR/LatAm FX forwards (1M-12M) with Spanish credit counterparties under ISDA 2002 / CSA
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or low-liquidity LatAm currencies (USD/MXN, USD/CLP, USD/PEN) executed via Banco de España licensed counterparties
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD CCS) for term-liquidity matching on capital injections
FX swaps (spot/forward combinations) for short-term treasury netting and liquidity management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts (Cuentas Anuales) deposit with the Mercantile Registry, comprising Balance Sheet, Profit and Loss Account, Statement of Changes in Equity, and Management Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil (Company Register) of the province of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved by the shareholders' general meeting within six months of the fiscal year-end and deposited within one month of approval; for a 31 December year-end the deposit is due no later than 31 July, with registry receipt by 30 July in standard practice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit is sanctioned by the Institute of Accounting and Auditing (ICAC) with fines from EUR 1,200 to EUR 180,000; after two consecutive years of non-deposit the Mercantile Registry orders cierre registral (closure of the company's file), suspending all further corporate registrations and effectively blocking operational filings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax return (Modelo 200) including annual report of taxable income, deductions, tax credits, and final corporate tax payable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed within six months and 25 days after the end of the tax period; for a 31 December year-end, the filing window is 1-25 July in the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers surcharges of 5%, 10%, 15% or 20% of the tax due depending on delay (3, 6, 12, or more than 12 months), statutory late-interest on unpaid amounts, and a fixed administrative penalty of EUR 1,500 per return; persistent non-filing enables AEAT compulsory assessment and embargoes

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Economic Activities Census maintenance confirmation (Modelo 036/037) verifying continued activity under the national tariff for professional and immigration advisory services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing obligation rather than a fixed annual filing; any change of activity, registered office, or relevant fiscal data must be submitted within ten calendar days of the event; where data are unchanged no separate annual confirmation is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update the census is an administrative infringement punishable by fines of EUR 400 to EUR 1,000 per instance; inaccuracies may also trigger AEAT rebuttal of the IAE exemption for newly formed entities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalization (diligenciado) of annual accounting books, members' register, and minutes book in the Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil corresponding to the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual accounting books must be presented for legalization within four months following the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the deadline is 30 April; corporate books are legalized upon opening and continuously maintained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Accounting books not legalized lose evidentiary value of reliability before courts and auditors; the registry may impose sanctions and the company's directors face liability for deficient corporate record-keeping under the Capital Companies Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual related-party transaction statement (Modelo 232) disclosing operations with shareholders, directors, and related entities where the amounts exceed EUR 100,000 or represent more than 1% of net equity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing window identical to Modelo 200: by 25 July following a 31 December fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission or inaccuracy constitutes a tax reporting infringement subject to fixed sanctions of EUR 300 per data record with a EUR 1,500 minimum per return; deliberate failure may be recharacterized as a serious tax offense with penalties up to 50% of the undetected tax base

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is compulsory when the SL meets at least two of the following three conditions on two consecutive balance-sheet dates: total assets exceeding EUR 4,000,000; net annual turnover exceeding EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees exceeding 50. Audit is also mandatory for entities with listed securities, public-interest entities, and members of a group required to present consolidated accounts; an audit may also be required by shareholders representing 5% of capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) approved by Royal Decree 1514/2007, aligned with EU IFRS for individual accounts; consolidated financial statements of groups apply IFRS-EU; accounts must be expressed in euros and give a true and fair view

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain has no standalone annual UBO form for an SL; beneficial owners holding more than 25% of share capital or exercising control must be identified in the Registro de Titularidades Reales (regulated by Law 10/2010 on AML) with every material change submitted within ten days. Any transfer of quotas in the SL must be executed before a notary, communicated to the company, and annotated in the Register of Members; transfers not recorded in the corporate register are not opposable to third parties. The company must maintain a current beneficial-ownership map annually in support of its AML-KYC obligations and SEPBLAC inspections, and confirm the absence of changes in each annual general meeting.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Administradores)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 330-980 (EUR 300-900) per year for commercial registered-office or corporate-agent services in Madrid or Barcelona for an SL providing immigration visa advisory services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000-8,000 (EUR 2,500-7,000) for a statutory audit engagement of an SL that exceeds the small-company audit exemption thresholds; small exempt entities pay no audit fee unless a shareholder or financing counterparty requires review

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly incorporated companies generally apply a 15% rate during the first profitable tax period and the immediately following profitable tax period, subject to statutory exclusions and anti-abuse rules. Qualifying micro-enterprises and small companies may benefit from reduced rates under the applicable annual tax legislation. Spanish tax residents are generally taxed on worldwide income; non-residents are taxed under the Non-Resident Income Tax regime on Spanish-source income. The standard VAT rate applicable to ordinary advisory services is generally 21%, subject to place-of-supply and exemption rules.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite. Spanish corporate tax losses may generally be carried forward without a fixed expiry period, subject to utilization limits, ownership-change restrictions, anti-abuse provisions, and the statutory turnover-based percentage caps.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Spanish State Tax Administration Agency (AEAT) electronic headquarters using an electronic certificate, Cl@ve where permitted, or an authorized tax representative. Modelo 220 applies where the company belongs to a Spanish consolidated tax group.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is due within the first 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer ending on 31 December, the normal deadline is 25 July of the following year. If the deadline falls on a non-business day, the applicable electronic filing rules extend it to the next business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Spanish tax identification number (NIF), registered address, tax period start and end dates, legal form, activity classification, tax regime, and filing-status indicators.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder or parent is not entered as the taxpayer where the Spanish SL is a separate Spanish tax resident. Enter the SL's own NIF and registered address. Report non-resident ownership in the relevant related-party, shareholder, and beneficial-owner sections.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before tax derived from statutory accounts prepared under Spanish accounting rules or an accepted accounting framework, reconciled to the tax computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude the non-resident parent's worldwide income. Include only the Spanish SL's accounting result and properly attributable Spanish business income and expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary adjustments for non-deductible expenses, depreciation, provisions, impairments, finance-cost limitations, exempt income, valuation differences, related-party adjustments, and other Corporate Income Tax reconciliation items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not deduct shareholder, parent-company, or foreign-head-office costs unless they are genuine, documented, economically connected to the Spanish business, and allocated on an arm's-length basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses from prior periods used in the current year, including the applicable utilization limitation and remaining balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses remain attributable to the Spanish legal entity. They cannot be transferred to a foreign shareholder or offset against foreign-group profits unless a legally applicable Spanish consolidation or restructuring regime applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adjustments, loss utilization, tax credits, and the applicable statutory or incentive rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the ordinary Spanish SL rate unless the company independently qualifies for a reduced rate. A foreign shareholder's residence does not create a reduced Spanish corporate tax rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Withholdings, prepayments, and payments on account
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate tax prepayments, withholding tax credits, installment payments under Modelo 202, and other permitted credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Spanish withholding tax on payments received by the SL may be credited only where legally attributable to the SL and supported by withholding certificates. Foreign tax credits require statutory conditions and documentary evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable deductions for research and development, technological innovation, employment, qualifying investments, donations, double-tax relief, and other statutory incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only incentives earned by the Spanish SL. Foreign-group expenditure, foreign employees, and foreign research activities do not qualify merely because the shareholder is connected to the SL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable, refundable amount, zero liability, installment application, bank account, payment method, and direct-debit instructions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The taxpayer or authorized representative must ensure that the Spanish bank account, payment reference, and electronic authorization are valid. Tax payable remains the SL's obligation even where the parent funds the payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information concerning transactions with shareholders, directors, group companies, foreign affiliates, and other related parties, including amounts and transaction categories.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose cross-border management fees, marketing fees, recruitment commissions, visa-processing support, loans, guarantees, royalties, and shareholder expenses. Reconcile disclosures to accounting ledgers, invoices, contracts, and transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ultimate beneficial owner, legal representative, tax adviser, and electronic filing authorization information where required by the form and AEAT systems.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the natural-person ultimate beneficial owner behind foreign corporate shareholders. Do not report only an intermediate holding company where beneficial-owner disclosure is required.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without tax payable may attract a fixed penalty generally starting at EUR 200, normally reduced by 50% where the statutory conditions for voluntary filing apply. Late filing with tax payable generally attracts a surcharge of 1% plus an additional 1% for each complete month of delay during the first 12 months; after 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus applicable late-payment interest. Formal tax infringements may generate penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of unpaid tax, depending on concealment, fraud, repeated conduct, or other aggravating factors.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, Corporate Income Tax installment-payment declaration, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters. Modelo 222 applies to entities within the consolidated tax regime.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly payment windows; generally due 1 to 20 April, October, and December, with the December payment due 1 to 20 December. Direct debit may have an earlier operational deadline.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Installment payments are generally made during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December. The applicable calculation method is normally based on the prior year's tax liability or, where elected or mandatory for qualifying large taxpayers, on the current-period accounting tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF, legal name, tax period, fiscal year, and applicable installment-payment regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish SL's details. The foreign shareholder is not substituted as the taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year corporate tax liability or current-period tax base, depending on the applicable calculation method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign parent profits and unrelated foreign tax positions. Include Spanish taxable operations and qualifying Spanish withholding credits only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory percentage applied to the relevant calculation basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm whether the company falls within the current-period method because of turnover, group status, or election. Group turnover may affect the applicable method even where the Spanish SL is individually small.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior installment payments and credits applied against the current installment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile amounts to AEAT payment records and the company's general ledger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net installment amount, payment method, bank account, or zero-payment declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the Spanish entity or authorized representative can complete electronic payment before the deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment may result in statutory surcharges generally ranging from 1% plus 1% per complete month during the first 12 months, to 15% after 12 months, together with applicable late-payment interest after the statutory threshold. Failure to make required installments can also generate interest, collection proceedings, and underpayment penalties after assessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 232, Informative declaration of related-party transactions and transactions with jurisdictions classified as non-cooperative or low-tax jurisdictions, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally filed during the eleventh month following the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the usual filing period is 1 to 30 November of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the counterparty, country, relationship category, transaction type, and aggregate transaction amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report foreign parent companies, subsidiaries, directors, common-control entities, and other related parties. Use the counterparty's foreign tax identification information where available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Goods, services, financing, guarantees, royalties, dividends, leases, restructuring, asset transfers, or other related-party transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify immigration referral commissions, student-placement services, visa-administration services, software access, marketing support, loans, and management charges according to their legal and economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross transaction amount, debit or credit direction, and transfer-pricing method or valuation basis where required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use amounts consistent with the statutory accounts, invoices, contracts, and Local File. Do not net unrelated revenue and expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transactions, holdings, financing, or payments involving jurisdictions included in the applicable Spanish non-cooperative jurisdiction lists or otherwise subject to enhanced disclosure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Review the current Spanish list at the filing date. A foreign jurisdiction's classification may change, and the analysis must consider both the counterparty and beneficial owner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Business restructuring and transfer of assets
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosures for qualifying restructurings, transfers of business functions, or transfers of assets, rights, or obligations involving related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose transfers of customer databases, trademarks, software, referral networks, or substantial functions to or from the foreign group where the statutory reporting conditions are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file, late filing, or materially incorrect informative declarations may generate fixed penalties under the General Tax Law, commonly calculated by the number of omitted or incorrect data points, subject to statutory minimums, maximums, reductions, and available voluntary-correction rules. Repeated or deliberately false reporting may support broader tax-evasion penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends and other profit distributions to non-residents, subject to exemptions, treaties, beneficial-ownership requirements, and anti-abuse rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Spanish SL should obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the foreign shareholder before the payment or otherwise retain evidence required by the applicable treaty and Spanish administrative rules. The payer normally applies the treaty rate at source only when the documentation, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, holding-period, and eligibility conditions are satisfied. If excess withholding is imposed, the recipient may generally seek a refund from AEAT using the applicable non-resident tax refund procedure, supported by the residence certificate, payment evidence, withholding certificate, ownership evidence, and treaty analysis. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may eliminate Spanish dividend withholding where the statutory ownership percentage, minimum holding period, subject-to-tax, legal-form, anti-abuse, and substance conditions are satisfied. A foreign holding company lacking economic substance may be denied treaty or directive benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Spanish domestic withholding is generally 24% for interest and royalties paid to non-residents outside the EU/EEA framework, and generally 19% for qualifying EU/EEA recipients, subject to applicable legislation, treaty provisions, and statutory exemptions. Interest and royalty payments between qualifying associated companies resident in EU Member States may be exempt under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive as implemented in Spain, provided the minimum ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, beneficial-ownership, and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied. Tax treaties commonly reduce withholding to rates such as 5%, 8%, 10%, or 15%, depending on the treaty, income category, recipient status, and beneficial ownership. Payments to related foreign parties require arm's-length pricing and documentation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File documentation is generally required for related-party transactions unless a statutory exemption applies. A commonly relevant exemption applies where the aggregate amount of transactions with the same related person or entity does not exceed EUR 250,000 at arm's-length value during the tax period, subject to transaction-type and anti-abuse limitations. Master File documentation is generally required for Spanish entities belonging to groups with consolidated net turnover of at least EUR 45 million, subject to statutory content and exemption rules. The EUR 250,000 threshold is not a general exemption from arm's-length pricing, accounting support, or the ability of AEAT to request documentation.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other internationally accepted methods and valuation techniques where the statutory methods are not reasonably applicable
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a separate United Arab Emirates-style or Cayman-style standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime. Economic substance is nevertheless material under Spanish transfer-pricing rules, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule, the conflict-in-application-of-tax-law doctrine, beneficial-ownership principles, the controlled foreign company regime, interest and royalty exemptions, treaty anti-abuse provisions, and the principal-purpose and anti-abuse standards applicable to EU and treaty relief. The Spanish SL should maintain genuine local functions, personnel or outsourced operational capacity under its control, premises or adequate operating infrastructure, decision-making, commercial risk assumption, customer contracts, bank-account control, and contemporaneous business records. A conduit company receiving funds and immediately remitting them to a foreign group member is at high risk of denied deductions, recharacterization, withholding-tax assessment, and penalty exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing advisory revenue, issuing false invoices, understating student or visa-service fees, fabricating deductible expenses, diverting customer payments to foreign accounts, or intentionally filing materially false Corporate Income Tax, VAT, payroll, or withholding returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax deficiencies may attract penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of unpaid tax, together with late-payment interest and collection costs. Serious tax fraud may constitute a criminal offense where statutory monetary thresholds and intent requirements are met, with fines and imprisonment under the Spanish Criminal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may face subsidiary liability for unpaid tax, civil restitution, disqualification from managing companies, and criminal liability. Travel restrictions or precautionary asset measures are not automatic but may be ordered in criminal or enforcement proceedings. Imprisonment is possible for qualifying tax crimes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False immigration, visa, or residence documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting forged admission letters, employment contracts, bank statements, accommodation evidence, identity documents, or false statements to Spanish authorities or foreign consulates; selling guaranteed visas; or knowingly facilitating unlawful immigration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential offenses include document forgery, fraud, false representation, and offenses against foreign nationals. Sanctions may include administrative fines, loss of authorization, cancellation of applications, civil damages, and criminal imprisonment depending on the conduct and evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, employees, and agents who knowingly participate may incur direct criminal and civil liability. The limited-liability status of the SL does not protect individuals from personal liability for their own fraudulent acts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Representing clients before authorities without required authorization, providing reserved legal services without qualified professionals, misrepresenting professional credentials, or operating a regulated placement or advisory activity without the applicable registration, authorization, or professional coverage.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Possible administrative fines, prohibition orders, invalidation of filings, consumer claims, professional disciplinary measures, and criminal exposure where unauthorized practice is combined with fraud or document offenses. The exact sanction depends on the activity, autonomous-community rules, and the authority involved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil damages, administrative disqualification, and criminal liability for knowing authorization breaches or fraudulent representation. Liability is not automatically eliminated by outsourcing work to contractors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to charge or account for Spanish VAT, incorrectly treating taxable advisory services as exempt education, using false VAT numbers, failing to issue compliant invoices, or claiming input VAT on private, fictitious, or foreign-parent expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of unpaid VAT, late-payment interest, and penalties commonly calculated as a percentage of the improperly unpaid, credited, or refunded tax. Serious or repeated fraudulent conduct may result in criminal tax proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur subsidiary tax liability for deliberately or negligently caused unpaid VAT and may face criminal exposure where the conduct satisfies tax-crime requirements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging excessive foreign management fees, referral commissions, royalties, or financing costs; allocating Spanish customer revenue to a foreign affiliate without functions or risk; or failing to document arm's-length pricing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may adjust the Spanish tax base, deny deductions, recharacterize payments, impose withholding tax, require interest, and impose transfer-pricing documentation or valuation penalties. Repeated or intentional concealment may trigger broader tax-evasion sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face subsidiary tax liability and, in deliberate fraud cases, criminal exposure. Personal liability is more likely where directors approved unsupported invoices, concealed beneficial ownership, or ignored professional advice and statutory records.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, conduit financing, or treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Spanish SL with no real business, personnel, operational control, or commercial risk solely to obtain treaty benefits, route dividends, receive foreign group funds, or create artificial deductible expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or EU directive relief, withholding-tax assessment, denial of expense deductions, recharacterization of transactions, interest, anti-abuse penalties, and potential criminal consequences where concealment or fraud is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil restitution, subsidiary tax liability, asset-securing measures, management disqualification, and criminal liability where they knowingly operated the structure as a conduit or sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party wire transfers, using personal or client accounts, failing to identify beneficial owners, ignoring sanctions or politically exposed person risks, structuring payments to avoid controls, or facilitating proceeds connected with fraud, corruption, or trafficking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Where the business is an obliged entity under Spanish Law 10/2010, failures may result in administrative sanctions including significant fines, public statements, temporary or permanent prohibitions, and management sanctions. Criminal money-laundering liability may include fines and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may face personal administrative and criminal liability for knowing participation, grossly negligent controls, concealment, or obstruction. Account freezes and travel restrictions may be imposed by competent authorities in relevant proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Holding visa, tuition, accommodation, or government-fee funds in company accounts without segregation, using client funds for working capital, falsifying refund records, or transferring funds to unrelated foreign accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential breach of contract, consumer-protection rules, fraud, misappropriation, or insolvency-related offenses; consequences may include restitution, damages, account freezing, administrative fines, and criminal penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unlawful diversion of entrusted funds, including civil restitution and criminal sanctions. Limited liability does not protect intentional misappropriation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying employees as contractors, paying undeclared commissions, failing to register staff, concealing payroll, or using foreign workers without the required authorization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Back payments of social-security contributions, employment-law fines, surcharge and interest, repayment of improperly obtained benefits, and possible criminal liability for serious contribution fraud or illegal employment practices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur subsidiary liability for unpaid social-security amounts and direct criminal liability for deliberate fraud, exploitation, or illegal-worker arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining off-book accounts, manipulating revenue recognition, concealing related-party transactions, filing false annual accounts, omitting the ultimate beneficial owner, or destroying accounting records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Possible accounting, corporate, tax, insolvency, and criminal sanctions, including financial penalties, director disqualification, rejection of tax deductions, and imprisonment for qualifying offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for creditor and shareholder losses, insolvency liability, disqualification, personal fines, and imprisonment where falsification or fraud is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing passports, bank statements, criminal-record certificates, student records, or immigration files without a lawful basis, adequate security, privacy notices, retention controls, or cross-border transfer safeguards.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GDPR and Spanish data-protection sanctions may include orders to stop processing, delete data, notify affected persons, and administrative fines up to the applicable GDPR maximums, subject to the infringement category and the controller's circumstances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The company is normally the primary regulated entity, but directors and managers may face civil, employment, or criminal liability for intentional misuse, obstruction, destruction of evidence, or unauthorized disclosure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying officials, agents, educational institutions, immigration intermediaries, or foreign public officials to accelerate applications, obtain unlawful approvals, suppress adverse information, or secure contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines, confiscation, procurement exclusions, corporate penalties, dissolution or judicial intervention in severe cases, and imprisonment for responsible individuals may apply under Spanish anti-corruption law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and employees may face direct criminal liability, civil restitution, asset confiscation, management disqualification, and possible travel restrictions during proceedings.
